links.outcome: Appropriate triage/urgency recommendations for simulated ophthalmic complaints across urgency levels
links.effect: Appropriate triage 90.0% overall; GPT-4 96.3% vs Bard 83.8% (p=0.008); potential harm 6.3% GPT-4 vs 20.0% Bard (p=0.010).
links.quote: GPT-4 performed better than Bard for appropriate triage recommendations (96.3% vs. 83.8%; p = 0.008), grader satisfaction for patient use (81.3% vs. 55.0%; p < 0.001), and lower potential harm rates (6.3% vs. 20.0%; p = 0.010).

links.outcome: Chatbot recognition of urgency and appropriate triage recommendation
links.effect: 90.0% appropriate triage overall; GPT-4 96.3% vs Bard 83.8%; harm rates 6.3% vs 20.0%, indicating some under-triage/potentially harmful advice.
links.quote: Chatbots were significantly better at ophthalmic triage than diagnosis (90.0% appropriate triage vs. 48.8% correct leading diagnosis; p < 0.001)

unlisted_practices: Providing more clinical descriptors in patient input improves chatbot diagnostic accuracy

screen.reason: Evaluates commercial LLMs (GPT-4 and Bard) on simulated ophthalmic patient complaints graded by ophthalmologists for triage and diagnosis accuracy, but does not test a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
